changes_requested — f1-tokens @ b5f30ce. Ten items. Read §0 first; it lists what is CORRECT and must NOT be re-done.

=== §0. WHAT IS CORRECT — DO NOT REDO OR "IMPROVE" ===
- All 14 DESIGN.md frontmatter colours are present in :root and byte-exact (0.90->0.9 and 0.50->0.5 are the same value). No invented colours. The one extra, --brass-hover: oklch(0.63 0.12 78), is legitimate — it is components.button-primary-hover. Keep the palette exactly as committed.
- Radius 2/4/8px correct; shadcn's 0.625rem is genuinely gone (0 occurrences of "0.625rem" in the production CSS, no --radius var at all). Spacing 8/16/32/64/120 correct. Type scale matches Hierarchy exactly incl. label +0.01em. --shadow-detached matches §4 verbatim.
- No .dark token block. The `@theme inline` + scoped `.ink-surface` approach is the right architecture and I verified it works: because of `inline`, `bg-muted-foreground` compiles to `var(--ink-muted)` at the use site, so redefining --ink-muted inside .ink-surface actually re-resolves. Dropping `inline` would silently break this. Keep it.
- The dark swaps that ARE there are correct: --brass-deep -> brass, --muted-foreground -> ink-muted-on-dark, --ring -> on-dark, --destructive -> destructive-on-dark, --success -> success-on-dark. I confirmed --ring:var(--on-dark) reaches the built CSS. Keep.
- Gate 1 (wdth) is genuinely PASS. Built @font-face carries font-stretch:62% 125%, h1 computes 125%, 1.28x measured. Correct and non-trivial.
- Gate 3 (tnum) is exemplary work. The fontTools analysis is right, the upstream cross-check is right, and refusing to substitute a font on your own authority was the correct call. Do not treat item 1 as a criticism of that.
- The Turbopack claim in item 5 of your evidence is TRUE and I confirmed it independently — see §2. You get credit for it; the bug is in the remedy, not the diagnosis.
- pnpm build / lint / verify:contrast all reproduce clean on my machine. The single lint warning is pre-existing in scripts/verify-contrast.mjs and untouched.

=== §1. BLOCKER — font swap: Golos Text -> Schibsted Grotesk ===
DESIGN.md was updated by Human Owner on 2026-07-22 (commit df42b0a) on the strength of your Gate 3 finding. Body font is now **Schibsted Grotesk**. The committed code still wires Golos_Text in layout.tsx, --font-golos in --font-sans, and a "Golos Text Fallback" @font-face. Replace all three.

Acceptance for the new Gate 3 — and this is the bar DESIGN.md now writes down explicitly, so meet it literally:
- Not "tnum is in the GSUB feature list". You already proved that check is worthless.
- Extract the ACTUAL SERVED woff2 that next/font emits into .next/static/media/ for Schibsted Grotesk (not a copy from Google, not the upstream ttf — the subset that ships).
- With fontTools, resolve the tnum single-substitution for all ten digits and print the advance width of each resulting .tf glyph.
- All ten advances must be ONE identical number. Spread must be exactly 0. Report the number and the spread.
- Then cross-check upstream google/fonts main as you did for Golos, so a future subsetting change can be distinguished from a source regression.
- Then confirm in the browser: per-digit rendered widths with font-feature-settings:"tnum" all equal, max delta 0.00px. Your existing per-digit harness is the right shape — reuse it.
If the spread is not zero, STOP and report — same as you did last time. Do not substitute.

=== §2. BLOCKER — the size-adjust fallback is dead code. Gate 2 is actually FAILING. ===
This is the one your evidence did not catch, and it is a real defect, not a nitpick.

Your diagnosis is correct: I confirmed Next 16.2.10 Turbopack does not emit next/font's adjusted fallback face. Zero ascent-override lines in the production CSS other than your two hand-written ones, and structurally the injection lives in build/webpack/loaders/next-font-loader/postcss-next-font.js — a webpack-only postcss pass that the Turbopack pipeline never runs. Good, hard-to-find finding.

But the remedy does not take effect. From the built CSS:
  --font-golos: "Golos Text", Helvetica Neue, sans-serif
  --font-archivo: "Archivo", Archivo, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif
  .font-sans -> font-family: var(--font-golos), "Golos Text Fallback", "Helvetica Neue", sans-serif
So the resolved stack is literally:
  "Golos Text", Helvetica Neue, sans-serif, "Golos Text Fallback", "Helvetica Neue", sans-serif
You passed fallback:["Helvetica Neue","sans-serif"] to next/font, which baked those INTO the variable, and then appended your override face AFTER them. `sans-serif` is a generic family — it always matches. Nothing after it is ever consulted. "Golos Text Fallback" and "Archivo Fallback" can never be selected by any browser. The metric override is inert; CLS is unprotected. Same defect on both faces.

Your browser proof did not catch this because font-gates-dom.html sets font-family:'Golos Text Fallback' DIRECTLY on the probe element. That proves the @font-face rule parses and the overrides apply when the family is named — it does not prove the family is reachable through var(--font-sans). Measure through the real cascade next time, not the isolated face.

Fix: the override face must sit immediately after the real family and BEFORE any generic. Either drop the `fallback` option from the next/font call so the variable contains only the real family, or stop appending and construct the whole stack yourself. Target:
  --font-sans: var(--font-schibsted), "Schibsted Grotesk Fallback", "Helvetica Neue", sans-serif
with --font-schibsted resolving to just "Schibsted Grotesk".

New metrics required — do NOT reuse the Golos numbers. From Next's own capsize table (next/dist/server/capsize-font-metrics.json), computed with Next's formula against Arial latin xWidthAvg 913/2048:
  Schibsted Grotesk: size-adjust 104.49%  ascent-override 93.46%  descent-override 24.67%  line-gap-override 0%
For reference, your Archivo numbers (98.7 / 88.96 / 21.28) and your Golos numbers (108.57 / 90.27 / 20.26) were both arithmetically correct — you sourced them properly. Keep Archivo's as-is; just fix its position in the stack.

Acceptance: a screenshot/measurement where an element styled with the ordinary `font-sans` utility, with the webfont blocked, renders at the adjusted metrics — i.e. proof through the cascade, not through a hand-named family.

Also: --font-display is `var(--font-archivo), "Archivo Fallback", Archivo, ...` where var(--font-archivo) already expands to `"Archivo", Archivo, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif`. Archivo appears three times. Clean it up while you are in there.

=== §3. HIGH — Ink Surface is incomplete. Two mandatory items are missing. ===
(a) DESIGN.md §2 Ink Surface: "Body text on it lifts to On Dark ... **with line-height raised by 0.05**." The .ink-surface block does not raise line-height. Add it (body 1.6 -> 1.65 inside the scope). This is a normative sentence, not a suggestion.
(b) --border stays var(--line) (oklch 0.90) inside .ink-surface. Line is specified as a 1.35:1 hairline on white; on Ink Surface the same value measures ~13.9:1 — a bright white rule where the system calls for a barely-there division. The spec table appears inside the dark process band, so this WILL ship visibly wrong.
DESIGN.md's Every-Surface Rule says every token that can appear on Ink Surface has a dark counterpart, but its frontmatter gives no dark Line and no dark Stroke. That is a SPEC GAP, not your call to fill. Do NOT invent values. Raise it to `lead` for Human Owner, get the two values written into DESIGN.md, then wire them. Note --input/--stroke is less urgent: stroke on ink measures ~4.6:1, which still clears 1.4.11, so it is survivable — but it should be decided, not defaulted.

=== §4. HIGH — focus ring does not meet the spec and is diluted below 3:1 ===
The base layer still carries shadcn's stock `outline-ring/50`, which compiles to `color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring) 50%, transparent)`. On white that is Ink at 50% alpha — roughly 1.9:1 against the surface, under the 3:1 that WCAG 1.4.11 / 2.4.11 require of a focus indicator. DESIGN.md §5 Buttons is specific: "Focus-visible draws a 2px ring offset 2px: Ink on light surfaces, On Dark inside an Ink Surface band."
Fix in globals.css (this is token/base-layer territory, so it is yours, not C1's): drop the /50 dilution and add a base :focus-visible rule at outline: 2px solid var(--ring); outline-offset: 2px. The .ink-surface override of --ring to on-dark then makes the surface decide the ring automatically, which is exactly what the spec asks for. Your verify:contrast row "onDark ring on dark 15.78:1" tests the token; it does not test the 50% alpha that is actually applied.

=== §5. HIGH — the Module Grid is a generic auto-fit grid with new names ===
DESIGN.md calls this the thing the brand actually owns and demands it be "visible, not merely underlying". What shipped is:
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(18rem, 100%), 1fr))
There is no cell, no 5:2, and nothing derived from the container footprint. Specifically:
(a) 18rem is an undeclared magic number with no derivation from anything in DESIGN.md.
(b) auto-fit means the column count is whatever happens to fit. Cell boundaries are therefore not addressable, so "hairline rules land on cell boundaries" and "process steps step across cells rather than sitting in equal thirds" are unimplementable on top of this primitive. Give the grid a determinate column count per breakpoint that collapses to one cell on mobile.
(c) cell-span-2 / cell-span-3 are unsafe on auto-fit: at narrow widths the track count drops below the span and the item creates implicit columns or overflows. DESIGN.md: "Where a layout cannot resolve to whole cells, the layout is wrong, not the grid" — so the primitive must make that impossible, not fail silently.
(d) --module-gap: var(--spacing-xs) is a flat 8px. The spec says the gutter is "proportional to the joining gap between stacked modules". Proportional means it scales with the cell, not a fixed pixel value. Either derive it as a ratio of cell width, or state plainly that 8px is an approved approximation and get that recorded — do not present a guess as a derivation.
(e) aspect-module-stacked: 5/4 has the same error. Two 5:2 cells stacked with a gutter g is 5 : (4 + g), not 5:4. Same in src/lib/grid.ts MODULE_ASPECT_STACKED.
(f) src/lib/grid.ts moduleWidth() is unused and recomputes in TS what CSS already knows. Delete it or justify a consumer.
Correct and keep: --aspect-module: 5/2 in the theme (it does generate a working `aspect-module` utility via the --aspect-* namespace) and the MODULE_CELL constant.

=== §6. MEDIUM — h3 is force-styled as a display face, contradicting the Title role ===
@layer base sets font-family:var(--font-display) AND font-stretch:125% on h1, h2, h3 together. But DESIGN.md Hierarchy assigns h3-shaped content — "Title (600, 1.125rem, 1.35): card headings, spec-group labels, form section headers" — to the BODY font, not Archivo Expanded. Card headings will render as expanded Archivo. The Balance Rule's "text-wrap: balance on every h1–h3" is about wrapping only; you over-extended it to family and width. Scope the display face + font-stretch to h1, h2 (and to an explicit display/headline utility); leave text-wrap:balance on all three.

=== §7. MEDIUM — the "no dark theme" prohibition is conventional, not structural ===
You removed the .dark token block, which was the ask. But Tailwind's stock `dark` variant is still live and media-based: the production CSS contains @media (prefers-color-scheme:dark) with eight dark:* utilities. They come from the untouched create-next-app page.tsx, so they are not your file — but it means the app currently does respond to OS dark mode, which DESIGN.md forbids. Since globals.css is F1's and only F1's, neutralise the variant there so this cannot creep back in via any later task, and note it in the commit. Making it impossible beats making it absent.

=== §8. MEDIUM — evidence methodology, so the next cycle's evidence actually proves something ===
(a) scripts/verify-contrast.mjs hardcodes the OKLCH triples in a JS object. It never reads globals.css. So "verify:contrast ALL PASS" proves DESIGN.md's palette is contrast-sound; it proves NOTHING about whether globals.css matches it. You cited it as token evidence. I had to diff all 14 values by hand. Recommend (coordinate with lead, the script is F0's file) making it parse globals.css so drift is actually detectable — otherwise this gate stays decorative for the whole project.
(b) The Gate 2 probe measured a hand-named family instead of the cascade — see §2. General rule for the rework: measure the thing as it will actually be used.
(c) globals.css and layout.tsx carry contradictory comments about the same fact — layout.tsx says "adjustFontFallback is on by default, emitting size-adjust/ascent-override metrics on the fallback face", globals.css says Turbopack does not emit it. The second is true. Fix the first.

=== §9. LOW — minor scope leakage ===
Scope discipline was otherwise good: three files, all inside tokens/font-wiring/grid. Two small leaks in layout.tsx: the h-full/antialiased and min-h-full/flex/flex-col layout classes belong to f4-shell. Harmless, but do not extend that. Correctly left alone: the placeholder metadata ("Create Next App"), which is x1-seo's.

=== §10. Note on next/font family naming ===
Turbopack registers the @font-face under the literal family name `Archivo` / `Golos Text`, not a hashed __Archivo_xxxx. A visitor with a system-installed Archivo could therefore shadow the served face. Not a defect and not blocking — just be aware when you interpret the next round of font measurements.

Resubmit with: the Schibsted binary tnum proof (all ten advances, one number, spread 0), the through-the-cascade fallback-metrics proof, and a note on §3's spec gap once lead has an answer.
